title: Uniqlo Set to Be World's Second-Largest Fashion Retailer
paragraphs: Japanese fashion company Fast Retailing, which owns Uniqlo, has announced revenue of $25 billion for its fiscal year, which ended on August 31.

This is higher than the annual revenue expected for Hennes & Mauritz AB, which owns H&M. The Swedish company is currently the world's second-largest mainstream casual fashion retailer — though that category excludes super-low-cost fashion like Shein and Temu.
Hennes & Mauritz — which also owns brands like COS, Arket and Other Stories — is only expected to announce revenue of $22.3 billion when its fiscal year ends in November.

Fast Retailing also announced a 32% rise in its annual profits, a record result for the fifth year in a row. Its strong results were driven by sales in North America and Europe, which were for the first time higher than sales in China, which had been the brand's largest market until now.

And the company isn't just happy to rise to number two. At a news conference in Tokyo, Tadashi Yanai, Fast Retailing's founder and CEO, was open about the company's ambitions, saying, "The goal of becoming global number one has been clear since our founding."
Getting to number one will still be a challenge, though — the current number one, Inditex and its Zara brand, posted revenue of $47 billion in 2025.

Yanai started his fashion business in Hiroshima in 1984, when he opened Unique Clothing Warehouse — a name that was later shortened to Uniqlo. Within 10 years, there were 100 Uniqlo stores across Japan, and today there are around 2,500 stores globally.
The brand is known for its focus on simple, high-quality, everyday clothing.

According to The Financial Times, Uniqlo President and CEO Daisuke Tsukagoshi said one of the brand's plans to drive sales is strengthening its "seasonless" clothing as climate change makes the weather more extreme and unpredictable.
"We used to structure our product range around the four seasons, but now the boundaries between seasons are changing," he said.
